title: CI/CD and Production Deployment
description: Deploy Prisma applications to Vercel, Docker, AWS, and configure automated GitHub Actions migration pipelines.

data.text: Automating your build and release pipeline ensures that database migrations execute reliably before the new application version begins serving user traffic. A robust CI/CD workflow validates TypeScript types, verifies schema formatting, and deploys migrations automatically.
On platforms like Vercel, `prisma generate` must execute before Next.js builds. You can configure this via the `postinstall` script in `package.json`.

data.title: package.json Build Configuration
data.content: Ensuring Prisma Client is generated upon every dependency installation.

data.title: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
data.content: Automated test, typecheck, and migration deploy pipeline.
data.code:
name: CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Verify Prisma Schema Formatting
        run: npx prisma format --check

      - name: Apply Database Migrations
        run: npx prisma migrate deploy
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}

      - name: Build Next.js Application
        run: npm run build

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `"postinstall": "prisma generate"` in `package.json` for reliable hosting builds.
Run `prisma format --check` in CI to enforce schema consistency across team branches.
Execute `prisma migrate deploy` in your release step prior to launching new app containers.
